evaluation_method: Compare fresh-agent performance with and without the skill per EVALUATION-GUIDE.md.

prohibited_failures: Popularity-based recommendation with no health/fit evidence

cases.name: Choose a job-queue library
cases.query: We need a background job queue for our Node service (retries, scheduling, ~1k jobs/min). Evaluate options and recommend one, or tell us to build.
files: access to inspect candidate repos and the existing stack (already runs Redis and Postgres)
baseline_risks: Recommends the most popular library on stars; ignores that the stack already has infra that could serve
expected_behavior: Sharpens must-haves (retries, scheduling, throughput) and weights them
Considers reusing existing Redis/Postgres-backed options and build
Health assessed via cadence/issues/maintainers with citations
Exit cost and an adapter mitigation noted; conditional recommendation

cases.name: Trivial capability, big dependency
cases.query: Should we add left-pad-style 'is-odd'/'is-even' style helper packages, or that 200-star 'deep-clone' package, for these small utilities?
files: the few call sites needing the trivial behavior
baseline_risks: Recommends adding the packages because they exist and are simple to install
expected_behavior: Weighs the supply-chain/maintenance liability against a few lines of owned code
Recommends do-without/build for the trivial cases
For deep-clone, checks whether the platform/stdlib already covers it
must_not: Add a dependency for behavior that is a few lines of stable code without noting the tradeoff

cases.name: License landmine
cases.query: Evaluate adopting this GPL-3.0 PDF library into our closed-source SaaS that we distribute as an on-prem binary to customers.
files: the library's license and the product's distribution model
baseline_risks: Evaluates only features/health; the copyleft-vs-distributed-binary conflict is missed
expected_behavior: Flags the GPL reciprocity conflict with on-prem distribution as a blocking concern
Recommends alternatives with compatible licenses or a service boundary, and legal review
Does not present features as decisive when licensing blocks adoption
must_not: Recommend adoption without surfacing the license conflict

cases.name: Abandoned incumbent, sunk-cost pressure
cases.query: We already depend heavily on 'oldframework'. Last release 3 years ago, original maintainer archived the repo, 600 open issues. Leadership says 'it still works, don't touch it'. Evaluate whether to keep it.
files: repo showing deep coupling to oldframework across many modules
baseline_risks: Endorses 'it still works' without weighing the abandonment/security risk and deep coupling
expected_behavior: Assesses the abandonment signals honestly (no releases, archived, security-response gap)
Quantifies the deep-coupling exit cost as the core problem
Recommends a risk-managed path (fork-readiness, adapter/strangler, planned replacement) with triggers, not blind status quo
must_not: Bless indefinite reliance on an archived, unmaintained core dependency without risk mitigation

cases.name: Design question, not dependency choice
cases.query: Should our caching layer use write-through or write-behind semantics?
baseline_risks: Skill could turn a design-semantics question into a library shootout
expected_behavior: Recognizes a design decision (first-principles-design/performance territory); no dependency comparison
must_not: Produce a dependency evaluation matrix for a caching-semantics question
